title: Extension bundles install without signature verification
description:
ExtensionInstaller.swift:46-64 installs any .crx/.xpi/.zip by stripping the CRX header (ExtensionArchive.swift:67) and writing the ZIP to disk; the CRX2/CRX3 signature is never validated and unsigned .xpi/.zip install with no provenance. Anyone who opens a malicious bundle runs its code with full extension privileges. WebKit provides no signing store, so the browser must check.

DECISION (2026-08-07): trust model is WARN-BUT-INSTALL. Unknown or missing signer is not blocked; the UI shows an unverified-developer warning before the bundle is enabled. Verified signatures from a pinned key are trusted silently. No paid Apple signing identity required.
design: Verify CRX2/CRX3 signatures against a pinned public key (store key or developer key); unknown/missing signer is allowed but flagged in the UI before enable. .xpi/.zip carry no signature, so they always take the warn path. Reuse ExtensionArchive byte parsing; keep bundle load path unchanged. Surface verification result (verified / unverified) on the extension row and in an install-time confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: CRX2/CRX3 signatures are actually verified against a pinned public key (not stripped-and-ignored); unsigned .xpi/.zip and unknown-signer bundles still install but the UI shows an unverified-developer warning at install and on the extension row, and they are not silently trusted; tampered bundles are detected and flagged; tests cover tampered, unsigned, valid, and unknown-signer bundles
close_reason: CRX2/CRX3 signatures verified at install in new BrowserCrypto package; warn-but-install UI (row icon, install message, enable confirmation); verdict persisted as <slug>.verification; 10 verifier + 4 installer + 3 UI tests; prepush green

title: Command bar: '?' prefix forces search
description: QoL #3. Typing '?golang.org' (or '? golang.org') in the command bar must ALWAYS search 'golang.org', never navigate. Kills the URL-vs-search misfire class (URLInput.resolve treats any single dot-token as a host, URLInput.swift:55). Pure ChordCore change: URLInput.forcedSearchQuery helper + first branch in CommandBarRanking.fallback, so the search path never enters resolve's navigate branch. Spec: docs/design/command-bar-search-prefix-and-top-sites.md.
acceptance_criteria: '?golang.org' yields one .search row, title omits the '?', URL is the search template; '?localhost' searches, never hits the localhost navigate rule; plain 'example.com' still navigates; URLInputTests forcedSearchQuery table + RankingTests pass.
close_reason: Implemented URLInput.forcedSearchQuery + first branch in CommandBarRanking.fallback; '?golang.org' forces search, never navigates. Tests green (696).

title: Full-featured Web Inspector (DevTools) for web developers
description:
WKWebView apps get no Inspect menu by default. Enable full Safari Web Inspector via WKPreferences developerExtrasEnabled (private KVC key, technically private API — fine for hobby browser, App Store risk).

Scope:
- Enable developerExtrasEnabled on webview config (per-config, not always-on in release)
- Dev-mode toggle: global vs per-space (decide in design)
- Keyboard shortcut Cmd+Opt+I (Safari convention) via menu item
- Right-click 'Inspect Element' context menu appears automatically from WebKit once flag set
- Inspector is always a detached NSWindow in WKWebView apps (cannot dock like Chrome DevTools)
- Panels: Elements, Console, Sources (debugger/breakpoints), Network, Storage, Responsive Design Mode, Graphics, Performance, Audits

Out of scope / not possible: Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), Puppeteer automation — WKWebView has no public CDP.

User context: works in incognito; useful while testing Netflix DRM/HDR streams.
design: Implement behind a dev-mode flag. Decide global vs per-space persistence. Add Develop menu or Settings toggle. KVC key: webView.configuration.preferences.setValue(true, forKey: 'developerExtrasEnabled') before load. Verify context menu item appears without extra code.
acceptance_criteria:
Right-click on any page shows 'Inspect Element' and opens Web Inspector to that node
Cmd+Opt+I toggles/opens inspector on active webview
Dev-mode toggle exists (decided global vs per-space) and release builds can disable
All standard panels functional: Elements, Console, Sources, Network, Storage, Responsive
close_reason: Dev-mode toggle (global, off by default, Settings > General + Develop menu). Engine sets developerExtrasEnabled per-view; Show Web Inspector (Cmd+Opt+I) via private _inspector KVC; Inspect Element context menu from WebKit once flag set. DRM Diagnostics panel behind same toggle.

title: YouTube page freezes after ad (no scroll, no click)
description:
User report: after an ad is skipped/fast-forwarded on first load, the whole watch page becomes non-interactable once the ad ends — no scroll, no click — until the tab is closed.

Root cause: skipping/rate-blasting an ad triggers YouTube's anti-adblock enforcement wall. YouTubeAdBlocker's CSS only hides the wall's dialog (tp-yt-paper-dialog:has(ytd-enforcement-message-view-model)); the wall is a modal iron-overlay whose open handler pins a full-screen tp-yt-iron-overlay-backdrop (swallows all pointer events) and sets body overflow:hidden (locks scroll). The overlay's close path never runs for a CSS-hidden element, so the page stays frozen after the ad.

Fix (YouTubeAdBlocker.swift): a MutationObserver dismantles the wall — removes ytd-enforcement-message-view-model (climbing to its TP-YT-PAPER-DIALOG host so the overlay stack isn't left with an orphan), removes a visible tp-yt-iron-overlay-backdrop, restores documentElement/body overflow, and best-effort resumes the paused player. Kept the CSS hide as fallback. Added test anchor YouTubeAdBlockerTests.dismantlesEnforcementWall. Verified: swift build -warnings-as-errors clean, full suite 602 tests green.
close_reason: Fixed: YouTubeAdBlocker now dismantles the enforcement wall (removes the iron-overlay backdrop + restores overflow) via MutationObserver instead of only CSS-hiding the dialog. Build clean, 602 tests green.

comments.author: Doddy Rizal Novianto
comments.text: Verified manually (2026-08-14): with the fix in place, skipping/fast-forwarding the pre-roll ad no longer freezes the page — scroll and clicks work after the ad ends. No regression in ad skipping or mute behavior.

title: Fix: YouTube fullscreen video renders black until app is relaunched
description:
User report: sometimes the YouTube player goes fully black in video fullscreen (YouTube's own fullscreen button). Exiting fullscreen (Esc/F) restores the normal page, but re-entering fullscreen is black again, and only quitting Chord fixes it. Reloading the tab does not help.

Root cause: macOS WebKit element-fullscreen reparenting bug (webkit.org/b/313802, reproduced on macOS 26). When a page element goes fullscreen, WKWebView is replaced by a placeholder, moved into a WebKit-owned fullscreen window, then moved back (WKWebView.fullscreenState docs). If the web view is AutoLayout-governed from an ancestor (SwiftUI hosting view), it comes back at a collapsed 0x0 frame and fullscreen video renders black persistently.

Fix (uncommitted, local):
- WebSurfaceContainerView.install: WKWebView now uses frame + autoresizing [.width,.height] instead of Auto Layout constraints (the documented workaround).
- LiveWebView observes WKWebView.fullscreenState; on .notInFullscreen it re-anchors the web view frame to the container bounds and forces a repaint, and logs every transition to the AppLog.

Verification: prepush green (601 tests). Needs a real-app pass: enter/exit YouTube fullscreen repeatedly, especially after the sidebar/pane is resized.
close_reason: User verified manually: black YouTube fullscreen no longer reproduces (2026-08-11). Fix shipped; see ADR 019.

title: Content-blocker weekly refresh is all-or-nothing across both lists
description: ContentBlocker.swift:104-112 concatenates EasyList + EasyPrivacy into one combined string; if either fetch fails the entire refresh aborts and defers to next launch (lastRefresh untouched), so one flaky URL costs both lists for a week. Also hashes/compiles them as one unit, so a change in one list invalidates the other's compiled chunks.
design: Fetch, hash, compile, and store each list under its own identifier (per-list shortHash); track lastRefresh per list; keep the seed fallback and the existing content-hash cache-hit behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A failure fetching EasyList does not lose an already-fetched EasyPrivacy update and vice versa; each list refreshes independently; compiled chunks are keyed per list so a change to one does not invalidate the other's cache
close_reason: ContentBlocker refreshes each list independently (per-list hash identifiers, per-list lastRefresh keys, failed list keeps last good set and retries); seed fallback for never-refreshed slots; legacy single-key migrated read-once; 11 engine tests incl. 3 new per-list; prepush green

title: Command bar: inline domain autocomplete
description: QoL #1. Chrome-omnibox-style prefix completion: type 'you', the bar suggests 'youtube.com' with the suffix highlighted; Enter confirms. Currently the ranker only fuzzy-matches STORED urls/titles (CommandBarRanking.swift) and never EXTENDS a typed prefix into a known domain; URLInput only navigates complete lookalike hosts. Sources: history domains + open-tab domains (no network). Needs its own design: where the completion text lives in CommandBarView, arrow-key semantics while a suffix is highlighted, dedupe against the existing navigate row. The named follow-up in docs/design/command-bar-search-prefix-and-top-sites.md.
design: DESIGN (2026-08-28): Chrome-style inline domain completion. ChordCore: Suggestion gains an optional 'completion: String?' (untyped suffix, default nil). New autocomplete source in CommandBarRanking: on a non-empty, space/slash-free query, collect known dot-domains from history hosts + open-tab hosts (no network), pick the lexicographically-first that the trimmed lowercased query is a strict prefix of, and emit one .navigate(url: https://domain) row with completion = leftover suffix. Scored completionBias(500) so it ranks just below the fallback. Dedupe vs navigate: fully-typed domains (suffix empty) never match, so resolve/navigate fallback owns them. UI (CommandBarView/CommandBarRow): when completion != nil, title renders as prefix + dimmed suffix. Arrow keys move row highlight normally (no special state); selecting the autocomplete row and pressing Return navigates to the completed URL. Typing past the prefix naturally clears it (prefix no longer matches). Accepts: prefix -> domain+highlighted suffix; Return on it navigates; divergence clears.
acceptance_criteria: Typing a prefix of a known domain (from history or open tabs) shows the domain with the untyped suffix highlighted; Enter navigates to the completed domain; typing diverges from the suggestion clears it.
close_reason: Added Suggestion.completion + autocomplete source (history/open-tab domains, completionBias 500); CommandBarRow dims the untyped suffix; Return navigates to completed URL. Tests green (705).

title: Command bar: top sites on empty query
description: QoL #2. Opening the bar with an empty query currently shows only open tabs (history/archived/commands/fallback all guard query.isEmpty in CommandBarRanking.swift). Add a topSites(input:limit:6) source, active only on empty query, scoring cachedHistory (already per-Space, already loaded) with the exact history formula (min(visitCount*3, visitCountMax) + recencyBonus). Rows are .history so activate()/UI untouched. Private windows lose it for free (store passes history: []). Spec: docs/design/command-bar-search-prefix-and-top-sites.md.
acceptance_criteria: Empty query shows top sites below open tabs, ordered by visit count, bounded at 6; empty history -> no rows; private window -> none; existing RankingTests pass.
close_reason: Added topSites source (history formula, base 0, limit 6) active only on empty query; factored shared historySuggestion builder. Tests green (699).

title: User-Agent freshness audit (track Safari version)
description:
Netflix and other DRM providers negotiate stream quality (resolution/bitrate/HDR) based on the User-Agent and capability signals the browser sends. WKWebView UA is derived from Safari; when Safari upgrades, the UA string in Chord may fall behind, causing services to downgrade or refuse streams.

Scope:
- Audit current WKWebView UA vs latest Safari version on this macOS
- Determine how UA is produced (default WKWebView UA vs custom override in Chord)
- Add a check/alert or scheduled maintenance item to bump UA on Safari/macOS updates
- Document expected UA format and where it lives in the codebase

Relation: WebKit upgrade workflow is covered by chord-browser-maintenance; this is the UA-specific slice.
design: Grep codebase for customUserAgent / UA overrides. Compare default WKWebView UA (WebKit version baked by SDK) vs Safari shipping UA. Document in maintenance skill or ticket. Only override if a real downgrade is observed.
acceptance_criteria:
Current UA in Chord identified and compared against latest Safari UA for this macOS
Gap detection method documented (manual or automated)
UA location in codebase documented with bump procedure
DRM stream quality negotiation verified not downgraded by stale UA
close_reason: Audit: macOS/Safari 26.6.2; bumped safariVersionToken 26.5->26.6. Documented single-source-of-truth + bump procedure in maintenance skill.

title: DRM capability diagnostics panel
description:
Netflix removed its secret menus (debug overlay + netflix.com/testpatterns) in 2023. Add an in-app diagnostics panel for the Chord browser that reports DRM/streaming capability truth directly from the engine.

Runs navigator.mediaCapabilities.decodingInfo against the profiles Netflix actually uses:
- video/mp4 hvc1 (HEVC/HDR10) 4K
- dvhe / dvh1 (Dolby Vision)
- audio/mp4 ac-3 (5.1), eac-3 (5.1/7.1), mp4a.40.2 (AAC)
Also surface: playback error codes from webview (Netflix 2003 etc), HDCP chain warnings (DisplayLink docks / non-HDCP adapters silently cap to 720p).

Motivation: dev wants to distinguish 'browser can't do it' from 'Netflix won't serve it'. FairPlay movie playback already works (webkit-arc-like-browser-das context); this is verification tooling.

Consider extending to a hidden Dev menu (consistent with Web Inspector dev-mode work).
design: Reuse a hidden WKWebView or evaluateJavaScript on current webview to call navigator.mediaCapabilities.decodingInfo for a fixed profile matrix. Render results in an in-app window/panel. Hook webview media error events for error-code capture. Place behind Dev menu toggle consistent with webkit-arc-like-browser-das.
acceptance_criteria:
Panel shows per-codec supported/not with full capability details (HEVC, DV, AC-3, E-AC-3, AAC)
Panel shows playback error codes when DRM playback fails
HDCP/display-chain warning surfaced when applicable
Accessible without Netflix secret menus (own UI)
close_reason: DRM Diagnostics panel (Develop > DRM Diagnostics, Cmd+Opt+D): Netflix profile matrix (HEVC 4K HDR, DV dvhe/dvh1, AC-3, E-AC-3, AAC), HDCP display-chain probe, live media/EME error capture via DRMDiagnosticsMonitor.

title: Page zoom shortcuts (Cmd+-, Cmd++, Cmd+0)
description:
Standard browser keyboard shortcuts missing in Chord:
- Cmd+- : zoom out
- Cmd++ : zoom in
- Cmd+0 : reset to 100%
Full-page zoom (not text-only), same behavior as Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge.

WKWebView support: macOS 10.13+ webview has pageZoom (WKWebView.pageZoom) and magnification. Evaluate which to use:
- pageZoom: full-page zoom on the webview layer (0..1 scale)
- magnification: similar

Considerations:
- zoom level persistence per-space or global (decide in design, consistent with Web Inspector dev-mode ticket)
- show current zoom in UI? (e.g. status bar / menu tick) — optional
- touchpad pinch zoom behavior already native in WKWebView, unaffected
design: Wire Cmd+-, Cmd++, Cmd+0 as menu items with key equivalents (standard on macOS). Apply via WKWebView.pageZoom. Decide persistence model consistent with the Web Inspector dev-mode ticket (webkit-arc-like-browser-das). Verify against other Chromium-family behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
Cmd+- zooms out, Cmd++ zooms in, Cmd+0 resets to 100%
Zoom is full-page (layout/viewport level), not just font size
Zoom state persists per decision (global vs per-space)
Shortcuts work in incognito/private tabs too
close_reason: View menu: Zoom In Cmd+=, Zoom Out Cmd+-, Actual Size Cmd+0 via WKWebView.pageZoom, global persistence in Preferences, PageZoom ladder + store/engine tests.

title: Support web geolocation (Google/Apple Maps) via WKUIDelegate + CoreLocation
description:
Add navigator.geolocation support so Google Maps / Apple Maps web can request location.

Three layers, mirroring the existing camera/mic pattern:

1. Engine (permission gate)
- Add webView(_:requestGeolocationPermissionFor:initiatedByFrame:decisionHandler:) to the WKUIDelegate extension in Packages/Sources/ChordEngine/NavigationCoordinator.swift (~line 273), alongside requestMediaCapturePermissionFor.
- Add .geolocation to SitePermissionKind (Packages/Sources/ChordCore/SitePermission.swift).
- Add paneRequestedGeolocation to WebEngineDelegate protocol (Packages/Sources/ChordEngine/WebEngine.swift), reuse requestSitePermission per-origin ask-once + persistence.

2. App (OS consent / TCC)
- Info.plist: NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription.
- Request CLLocationManager.requestWhenInUseAuthorization() at launch in AppDelegate so the app appears in System Settings > Privacy > Location Services.
- Link CoreLocation.
- No sandbox entitlement needed (app is unsandboxed, same tradeoff as camera/mic in Chord.entitlements).

3. Caveat
- macOS WKWebView geolocation historically unreliable (WebKit bug 140208). The delegate was only promoted from private SPI to public API in Feb 2026 (WebKit PR #58447), so requires a recent SDK. Test early on maps.apple.com and google.com/maps. Fallback if WebKit won't deliver coordinates: intercept navigator.geolocation via a shim like NotificationBridge, serving position from the host CLLocationManager (the Electron-on-macOS approach).
design: Wire the new WKUIDelegate geolocation method into NavigationCoordinator, add SitePermissionKind.geolocation, extend WebEngineDelegate/TabStore exactly like paneRequestedMediaCapture. App layer: CLLocationManager auth request at launch + Info.plist usage string. Verify WebKit actually delivers position on macOS before committing; otherwise implement a navigator.geolocation shim bridging the host CLLocationManager.
acceptance_criteria: Site asks for location, user sees one per-origin prompt (first time), then remembered decision. maps.apple.com and google.com/maps resolve coordinates when granted. Denying per-origin blocks that site only. Works across Spaces (decision scoped per Space).
close_reason: Working: Google Maps geolocation confirmed in the field — per-origin prompt, OS TCC prompt, coordinates delivered via the navigator.geolocation shim + host CLLocationManager. Prepush green (638 tests, app builds).

comments.author: Doddy Rizal Novianto
comments.text: Implemented via WebKit geolocation SPI (private, declared in NavigationCoordinator — SDK has no public/private header for it; same approach as Orion). Store reuses the ask-once per-origin SitePermission path with new .geolocation kind. App: NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription, location entitlement for the WebKit child sandbox. 3 new store tests; prepush (build+637 tests+app build) green. Remaining: runtime verification on maps.apple.com / google.com/maps — confirm WebKit delivers position on this macOS/WebKit build.

comments.author: Doddy Rizal Novianto
comments.text:
Runtime test failed: 'Google Maps does not have permission to use your location', no TCC prompt — the SPI never fires on macOS. Root cause confirmed: WebKit's CoreLocation geolocation provider is iOS-only (WKGeolocationProviderIOS), so the UIProcess never routes geolocation to the delegate on macOS.

Pivoted to the documented fallback: navigator.geolocation shim (GeolocationBridge in ChordEngine) + host CLLocationManager (ChordLocationProvider). Ops over a with-reply handler: query (remembered decision, seeds permissions.query), request (per-origin ask-once via existing SitePermission path), position (one fix; triggers OS TCC prompt on first use). watchPosition polls in-page. SPI kept as belt-and-suspenders. 4 store tests; prepush green (638 tests, app builds). Needs re-test.

title: User-Agent version tokens are stale and internally inconsistent
description: WebKitEngine.swift:370 hard-codes 'Version/26.5 Safari/605.1.15' as the live UA suffix, while UserAgent.swift:34 prefills the Settings custom field with Version/17.5 (defaultTemplate) and the presets carry 17.5/126/127 too. The app advertises two different Safari versions, and the token is hard-coded so it drifts from the actual WebKit engine version over time. UA-vs-engine feature mismatch is itself a fingerprint signal.
design: Centralize the Safari version token in one constant (e.g. in BrowserCore next to UserAgent.swift) and have WebKitEngine.swift:370 + UserAgent.swift:34 reference it. Match the token to the SDK's shipped WebKit version.
acceptance_criteria: Live UA suffix and the Settings prefill/template come from one source of truth and cannot drift; version matches the shipped WebKit/Safari token; existing unit tests for UserAgentRules and UA application still pass
close_reason: UserAgentPreference.safariVersionToken is the single source of truth; defaultTemplate builds from it and WebKitEngine.safariUserAgentSuffix references it; new BrowserCore + BrowserEngine tests pin the invariants; prepush green

title: YouTube ad sometimes not skipped or fast-forwarded
description: YouTubeAdBlocker tick() fails intermittently: an ad plays to the end instead of being skipped/fast-forwarded. Suspected causes in Packages/Sources/BrowserEngine/YouTubeAdBlocker.swift: (1) once-only playbackRate bump that YouTube's player resets to 1x, (2) skip-button click returns early and swallows the fallback seek/blast when the button is disabled/custom, (3) targets only the first <video> while YouTube A/B-tests ads on a separate element and the watch page has an ambient background video.
close_reason: Re-assert playbackRate every tick (YouTube resets it to 1x, so the once-only bump died), removed the early-return after skip-click so the seek/blast fallback always runs, blast every <video> instead of the first, and seek-to-end only when duration is ad-length (<=60s) so stitched ads can't skip the content.

title: Command bar: URL heuristic polish
description: QoL #4. Sharpen URLInput.looksLikeHost (URLInput.swift:55): add a TLD table so 'foo.grok' type gibberish stops navigating to a DNS error; handle a 'www.' prefix; decide whether single-word intranet hosts ('nas', 'myserver') navigate or search. Deliberately conservative today; the change must not regress the common 'example.com' navigate or multi-token search cases. Needs its own acceptance corpus (like LoginFormClassifier's captured-markup approach): a table of inputs -> expected navigate/search.
design: DESIGN (2026-08-28): Sharpen URLInput.looksLikeHost while staying conservative. 1) TLD table: the final label must be in a curated set of common generic + country TLDs instead of 'any all-letter label' — so 'foo.grok' stops navigating to a DNS error. 2) www prefix: strip a leading 'www.' before judging the TLD, so 'www.example.com' still navigates but 'www.grok' searches. 3) Intranet single-word hosts ('nas','myserver'): kept as SEARCH (conservative) — current behaviour, and 'no navigation for anything that would 100% DNS-fail'. 'localhost' remains the sole single-word navigator. Corpus (captured-style table) in URLInputTests: inputs -> isSearch(true=search,false=navigate). No UI/store/engine change; pure ChordCore.
acceptance_criteria: A corpus table of typed inputs -> navigate|search, incl. 'www x', TLD gibberish, intranet words; all existing URLInputTests still pass; no navigation for anything that would 100% DNS-fail.
close_reason: Replaced 'any all-letter label' with a known-TLD table; strip leading 'www.'; intranet single-words stay search; localhost sole navigator. Corpus table in URLInputTests (11 cases). Tests green (700).

title: Command bar: '@site' site search
description: QoL #5. '@gh swift' searches GitHub, '@so' StackOverflow, etc. Needs a small site registry (name, aliases, search URL template) + URLInput/ranker parsing for a leading '@' token. Developer-oriented; medium build. Independently testable: table of '@alias query' -> engine URL. Do after the ?-prefix lands (same parse layer).
design: DESIGN (2026-08-28): '@site' site search. ChordCore-only, reuses the ?-prefix parse layer. New pure-data SiteRegistry (file ChordCore/SiteRegistry.swift): entries {name, aliases[], urlTemplate with %s} — GitHub(gh), Stack Overflow(so), npm, Wikipedia(w/wiki), YouTube(yt). URLInput.siteSearchQuery(raw:) -> (alias, query)? when the trimmed text starts with '@' and there is a non-empty alias and a non-empty query; nil otherwise (falls through, like '?' alone). CommandBarRanking.fallback checks site-search right after forced-search: '@gh swift' -> .search row with the registry engine URL (via URLInput.search %s substitution); unknown alias -> nil -> normal resolve/search fallback. Title 'Search <Name> for "<query>"'. Unit tests: URLInput.siteSearchQuery table + SiteRegistry alias resolution (case-insensitive) + ranking table '@alias query' -> engine URL + unknown-alias fallback.
acceptance_criteria: '@alias query' opens the registered site's search URL for query; unknown alias falls back to normal search; registry entries are pure data, unit-tested.
close_reason: Added pure-data SiteRegistry + URLInput.siteSearchQuery parse layer; fallback dispatches '@alias query' to the site engine, unknown alias falls back to normal search. Tests green (710).

title: Command bar: '!' bangs and mid-typing engine switch
description: QoL #6. Firefox/DuckDuckGo-style: '!ddg query' forces a specific search engine, '!w query' Wikipedia, etc. Long tail of the '@site' registry work (#5) - shares the parse layer and registry. Niche; lowest priority in the QoL list.
design: DESIGN (2026-08-28): '!' bangs share the @site parse layer and registry, resolved consistently. Generalize URLInput.siteSearchQuery -> URLInput.dispatchQuery(raw:) accepting BOTH leading '@' and '!' (same alias/query split, same fall-through rules). Extend the pure-data SiteRegistry with search-engine entries so '@' and '!' resolve through the SAME entry(forAlias:) — a conflict (e.g. 'w' in both) lands on the same row, no divergence. New engine entries: Google(g), DuckDuckGo(ddg), Bing(bing), Brave(brave); existing sites unchanged. fallback dispatches '@alias' and '!alias' identically -> .search row with the entry's %s template URL; unknown alias -> normal search. Precedence: '?' forced-search first, then '@'/'!' dispatch, then resolve. Title 'Search <Name> for "<query>"'. Tests: parse table for '!', bang->engine URL table ('!ddg swift'->duckduckgo, '!w x'->wikipedia), consistency ('@gh'=='!gh' same URL), unknown-bang fallback.
acceptance_criteria: '!alias query' searches via the alias's engine; conflicts with '@' resolved consistently; unit-tested alongside #5.
close_reason: Generalized dispatchQuery to '@' and '!'; extended SiteRegistry with engine entries (Google/DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave); '@' and '!' resolve through the same registry. Tests green (714).

title: Passkeys: blocked until paid Apple membership, then system WebAuthn
description:
Goal: passkeys (WebAuthn) work in Chord. Measured 2026-08-28 on the free personal team (74XUPW85K2): Automatic signing refuses com.apple.developer.web-browser ('Entitlement not found and could not be included in profile'), so WKWebView has no platform authenticator and system passkeys are unavailable. Recorded in docs/design/password-vault.md.

Three paths, in order of preference:
1. SYSTEM (recommended once paid): add com.apple.developer.web-browser entitlement, build Release, verify PublicKeyCredential.isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable() returns true on an HTTPS page, then Register/Login on https://webauthn.io/ raises the Touch ID sheet. Works for any site, no extension involved. Unblocks the moment a paid account signs the app.
2. BITWARDEN VAULT: impossible. WebKit's WKWebExtensionController exposes no authenticator hook; Bitwarden's ceremony uses hybrid CTAP2/native-messaging WebKit doesn't implement; its MV3 build also dies at startup (chrome.offscreen). Do not pursue.
3. OWN-CEREMONY SHIM (only subscription-free path, not scheduled): main-world navigator.credentials override (pattern: GeolocationBridge, WebKitEngine.swift:304) bridging to a WebAuthn ceremony in ChordSecrets (WebCrypto: CBOR, COSE, ECDSA/Ed25519). High trust-surface; ADR 016 deferred on security grounds. No entitlements needed.
design: See docs/design/password-vault.md ('No passkeys' bullet) and the path notes in the description.
acceptance_criteria: With a paid membership, com.apple.developer.web-browser is provisioned and isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable() returns true on webauthn.io in a Release build.
